A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, title, smoothness framework, and warm-up experiments. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison despite substantial theoretical revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original curvature measurements and warm-up experiments on FineWeb and ImageNet-32, plus seed, optimizer, and hyperparameter analyses in Appendix I.

after.justification: v2 retains original language and vision experiments and adds initialization-dependent curvature measurements in Figure 2 and Appendix K.2.

M1.justification: The adaptive GD/SGD updates and practical schedule eta_k / max{1, f_batch(w_k)/C} are retained. The added transformer architecture is a theoretical example, not a replacement or new component of the proposed warm-up procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate FineWeb language modeling and ImageNet-32 classification. The new initialization study reuses the 70M FineWeb model. In-context learning appears as theoretical analysis; CIFAR-10 and Tiny Shakespeare are discussed only in relation to prior work.

E2.justification: The evaluated warm-up comparators remain tuned linear warm-up and no warm-up for both language and vision experiments. The expanded discussion of Liu et al. [2025] does not introduce an experimentally evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The added 70M diagnostic compares depth-scaled and fixed-variance initialization with clipped SGD at fixed learning rates 10^-4, 10^-3, and 10^-2. Existing benchmark settings and tuning grids are retained. Clipping at 1 was already disclosed in v1 Appendix I, so its addition to main-text descriptions is not a protocol change.

E4.justification: Figure 2 and Appendix K.2 add a focused initialization and learning-rate analysis examining initial curvature, the transition to sharpening, and later stability behavior. Existing seed variation, Adam verification, warm-up-length, and peak-learning-rate analyses are retained from Appendix I.

E5.justification: Both versions report means of three runs with min-max shading for the main performance experiments and retain the seed-variation analysis. No additional repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are reported.

E6.justification: v2 adds findings of higher initial curvature with depth-scaled initialization, a similar transition loss across settings, and approximately 20% of total loss reduction occurring during initial curvature reduction. Figure 5 slightly revises the linear-warm-up accuracy trajectory, and previously plotted training-loss trajectories are omitted. The language-model validation curves and principal performance conclusions remain.

T1.justification: v2 adds scalar-network curvature dynamics in Proposition 3.1, early-phase bounds for feedforward networks, and transformer/in-context results in Appendix E. It rewrites auxiliary lemmas, omits v1's separate regularized-MSE proposition, and changes Theorem 4.2's H0 coefficient from 20 to 40. Proposition D.1 also replaces v1 Proposition C.1's higher-power global bound with an affine statement, although its derivation still contains f(W)^(ell-1).

C1.justification: The central smoothness-based explanation and faster-convergence claim remain. v2 explicitly frames its main contribution around early curvature reduction and specifies the empirical claim as matching tuned linear warm-up and improving over no warm-up, refining v1's broader statements of practical usefulness.

C2.justification: Beyond v1's observation that the bound deteriorates after warm-up, v2 develops an account separating curvature reduction, progressive sharpening, and edge-of-stability behavior. It hypothesizes that depth-scaled initialization increases warm-up requirements and clarifies that fixed-step lower bounds concern stability across the function class. These substantially expand the mechanism and applicability discussion.

D1.justification: Appendix K.2 documents initialization formulas, affected MLP and attention-output weights, and clipping for the added diagnostic. Existing implementation references and configuration tables are retained: Tables I.1-I.2 become K.1-K.2 without substantive setting changes.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds curvature-dynamics positioning, while Appendix A expands into detailed comparisons with Liu et al. [2025] concerning architectural evidence, experimental scale, convergence assumptions, and empirical findings. New references support transformer theory, initialization effects, and optimizer connections; bibliographic publication updates are separate from these substantive additions.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction, smoothness motivation, theoretical discussion, and concluding section. It reorganizes architecture-specific analysis and appendices, introduces a scalar example before the smoothness definition, and adds an Impact Statement. This changes the narrative beyond merely inserting scientific results.

P2.justification: v2 adds initialization plots in Figure 2 and Figure K.1, combines v1's language-model validation and learning-rate plots into Figure 4, and removes training-loss panels from the main performance figures. Retained appendix plots are regrouped, and captions are revised; the configuration tables retain their structure.

improvement.justification: The early-phase explanation and initialization experiments improve the connection between theory and observed training behavior. However, v1 Proposition C.1 explicitly retained an f(W)^(ell-1) global bound, whereas v2 Proposition D.1 asserts an affine bound despite deriving higher-power terms immediately before Eq. (27). This unresolved mathematical inconsistency offsets the clearer exposition and added evidence, preventing a reliable net quality judgment for this theory-centered paper.
